invention.quote: or "spontaneity," often associated with the state of potentiality

defects.detail: 'When a child feeds upon its dead mother' for 子食於其死母 (piglets suckling, per reference)
'Those who are still in the womb, their repeated lack of action' renders the OCR garble 胎者之屢 (the amputee's shoes) fluently
'buried by the state' for 其人之葬也 (their burial); 'the eyes are as if they have all been abandoned' for 眴若皆棄之
'cannot be made to return to a state of bodily wholeness' splits 不得復使。形全 wrongly; 'carry out intentions' garbles 為爾
'The child si to feed its offspring at its dead mother' / 'all who look cast it aside' for piglets abandoning their dead mother
'The embryos that miscarry repeatedly' for OCR 胎者之屢 (刖者之屨, the footless man's shoes)
'must not cause her to serve again' — 取妻者 is the man who takes a wife, not the wife
'sufficient to cause meaning' / 'Beneath the meaning it continues' garble 足以為爾 / 意下又是

invention.quote: how much more so for one whose virtue is whole?

defects.detail: 'how much more so for one whose virtue is whole' is 況全德之人乎, which opens the next page
'buried without their armaments' for 不以翣資 (plumes; OCR 妾)
'A child feeding at the breast of its deceased mother... the eyes seem to abandon it all' for piglets fleeing
'Those who are pregnant repeatedly do nothing to love them' for OCR 胎者之屢無為愛之
margin 'then nothing is worth loving' for 即不足愛; 'sufficient to be of purpose' garbles 足以為爾
'run off without looking back' for 不見己焉爾 (she no longer saw them); margin has it right
'decorative burial plumes or sacrificial gifts of concubines' doubles 翣 and the OCR's 妾
'A son who feeds upon his dead mother... all those who look at her... abandon her' for piglets fleeing
'buried by their compatriots' for 其人之葬也
'Fetuses have repeatedly been treated without love' for OCR 胎者之屢 (the amputee's shoes)
'Those selected from among married women remain outside' for 取妻者止於外 (a newly married man)
margin 'lack martial vigor, therefore they are not suitable for concubines' for 無武故不資以妾

reason: Source (with OCR errors 妾 for 翣, 胎/屢 for 刖/屨) is Zhuangzi's piglets/dead-sow passage; T3 and T5 read it as the reference does (piglets, plumes/arms, amputee's shoes, newly married man), T3 adding next page's 況全德之人乎; T1/T2/T4/T6 render 子 as a child feeding on its mother and fluently translate the 胎者 garble as embryos/pregnancy, T6 also turns the bridegroom into married women.
